description: Sunrise and sunset against published almanac times for Kathmandu. Covers both horizon conventions the engine supports: the sea-level horizon used by Nepali published panchang, and the elevation-adjusted horizon Drik Panchang uses.

source.authority: Drik Panchang; Nepali published panchang (Gaurishankar meridian convention)
source.reference: Values carried forward from tests/test_horizon_dip.py and tests/test_nepal_patro_sun.py, where they were established while fixing the valley-dip regression (panchanga_cache payload-version log entry 21).
source.verified_by: Repository history: the sea-level pair is what published Nepali panchang shows and is the shipped default; the 1400 m pair reproduces Drik Panchang for the same chart.
source.notes: Two rows, one chart, two horizon conventions - this dataset exists to pin that the choice is deliberate. Feeding Kathmandu's real 1400 m elevation gives a ~1.1 degree sea-cliff dip that is unphysical in a valley ringed by hills; sea level is the shipped default.
source.convention: Geocentric apparent sunrise/sunset, upper-limb with standard refraction, Swiss Ephemeris rise_trans_true_hor. Two horizon models are compared explicitly: sea-level (h=0), which is the Nepali published-panchang convention and the engine default, and elevation-adjusted (h=1400 m geometric dip), which is what Drik Panchang applies. Local civil time, Asia/Kathmandu.

tolerance.rationale: Published almanacs print to the minute, and independent publishers differ slightly in refraction model and horizon definition. 90 s accepts a one-minute printed difference plus rounding, while still catching the ~380 s error the valley-dip bug produced.

entries.note: Sea-level horizon - the shipped default and the published Nepali panchang convention.
Elevation-adjusted horizon - reproduces Drik Panchang. Opt-in, not the default.
